28856-donald-and-dorothy.title: Donald And Dorothy
28856-donald-and-dorothy.creator: Unknown
28856-donald-and-dorothy.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The door of the study was closed, and only Nero was to be seen. He, poor dog, stood in the wide hall gazing wistfully at the knob, and pricking up his ears whenever sounds of movement in the room aroused his hope of being admitted. Suddenly he gave a yelp of delight. Somebody surely was approaching the door.

71527-14000-miles-a-carriage-and-two-wom.title: 14000 Miles A Carriage And Two Women
71527-14000-miles-a-carriage-and-two-wom.creator: Unknown
71527-14000-miles-a-carriage-and-two-wom.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. “We were a jolly pair, we two, and ladies at that; and we had decided to go, amid the protestations of the towns-people and the remarks of Madam Grundy that it was not proper, and that there were so many tramps it was not prudent for two ladies to take a trip with their horse and carriage along the North Shore.

arxiv-1810-01832.title: Two (Known) Results About Graphs with No Short Odd Cycles
arxiv-1810-01832.creator: Sariel Har-Peled, Saladi Rahul
arxiv-1810-01832.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Sariel Har-Peled, Saladi Rahul. Consider a graph with n n vertices where the shortest odd cycle is of length > 2 ​ k + 1 >2k+1 . We revisit two known results about such graphs: (A) Such a graph is almost bipartite, in the sense that it can be made bipartite by removing from it O ⁡ ( ( n / k ) ​ log ⁡ ( n / k ) ) O\bigl((n/k)\log(n/k)\bigr) vertices.

arxiv-2104-00623.title: Overscreening and Underscreening in Solid-Electrolyte Grain Boundary Space-Charge Layers
arxiv-2104-00623.creator: Jacob M. Dean, Samuel W. Coles, William R. Saunders, Andrew R. McCluskey, Matthew J. Wolf, Alison B. Walker, Benjamin J. Morgan
arxiv-2104-00623.description: Abstract Polycrystalline solids can exhibit material properties that differ significantly from those of equivalent single-crystal samples, in part, because of a spontaneous redistribution of mobile point defects into so-called space-charge regions adjacent to grain boundaries. The general analytical form of these space-charge regions is known only in the dilute limit, where defect–defect correlations can be neglected.

arxiv-2106-07493.title: Volume asymptotics and Margulis function in nonpositive curvature
arxiv-2106-07493.creator: Weisheng Wu
arxiv-2106-07493.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Weisheng Wu. In this article, we consider a closed rank one C ∞ C^{\infty} Riemannian manifold M M of nonpositive curvature and its universal cover X X . Let b t ​ ( x ) b_{t}(x) be the Riemannian volume of the ball of radius t > 0 t>0 around x ∈ X x\in X , and h h the topological entropy of the geodesic flow.

arxiv-2205-09176.title: Characteristics of the Permanent Superhumps in V533 Herculis
arxiv-2205-09176.creator: McKenna Leichty, Peter Garnavich, Colin Littlefield, Rebecca Boyle, Paul A. Mason
arxiv-2205-09176.description: Abstract We analyze two sectors of TESS photometry of the nova-like cataclysmic variable star V533 Her. We detect a periodicity consistent with the binary orbital period and estimate a revised value of 3.53709(2) hr. We also detect a strong signal near a period of 3.8 h that we associate with positive superhumps.

arxiv-2206-00965.title: Symmetry-protected higher-order exceptional points in staggered flatband rhombic lattices
arxiv-2206-00965.creator: Yingying Zhang 1∗ , Shiqiang Xia 1∗† , Xingdong Zhao 1‡ , Lu Qin 1 , Xuejing Feng 1 , Wenrong Qi 1 , Yajing Jiang 1 , Hai Lu 1 , Daohong Song 2 , Liqin Tang 2♯ , Zunlue Zhu 1 and Yufang Liu 1
arxiv-2206-00965.description: Abstract Higher-order exceptional points (EPs), which appear as multifold degeneracies in the spectra of non-Hermitian systems, are garnering extensive attention in various multidisciplinary fields. However, constructing higher-order EPs still remains as a challenge due to the strict requirement of the system symmetries.

arxiv-2301-08299.title: Can Neutrino Self-interactions Save Sterile Neutrino Dark Matter?
arxiv-2301-08299.creator: Rui An, Vera Gluscevic, Ethan O. Nadler, Yue Zhang
arxiv-2301-08299.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rui An, Vera Gluscevic, Ethan O. Nadler, Yue Zhang. Sterile neutrinos only interact with the Standard Model through the neutrino sector, and thus represent a simple dark matter (DM) candidate with many potential astrophysical and cosmological signatures. Recently, sterile neutrinos produced through self-interactions of active neutrinos have received attention as a particle candidate that can yield the entire observed DM relic abundance without violating the most stringent constraints from X-ray observations.

arxiv-2305-09573.title: Walking the Walk of AI Ethics: Organizational Challenges and the Individualization of Risk among Ethics Entrepreneurs Conference: 2023 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency; June 12–15, 2023; Chicago, IL, USA 2023 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (F
arxiv-2305-09573.creator: Sanna J. Ali, Angèle Christin, Andrew Smart, Riitta Katila
arxiv-2305-09573.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sanna J. Ali, Angèle Christin, Andrew Smart, Riitta Katila. Amidst decline in public trust in technology, computing ethics have taken center stage, and critics have raised questions about corporate “ethics washing.” Yet few studies examine the actual implementation of AI ethics values in technology companies. Based on a qualitative analysis of technology workers tasked with integrating AI ethics into product development, we find that workers experience an environment where policies, practices, and outcomes are decoupled.

arxiv-2310-12157.title: Desynchronization of large-scale neural networks by stabilizing unknown unstable incoherent equilibrium states
arxiv-2310-12157.creator: Tatjana Pyragienė and Kestutis Pyragas
arxiv-2310-12157.description: Abstract In large-scale neural networks, coherent limit cycle oscillations usually coexist with unstable incoherent equilibrium states, which are not observed experimentally. We implement a first-order dynamic controller to stabilize unknown equilibrium states and suppress coherent oscillations. The stabilization of incoherent equilibria associated with unstable focus and saddle is considered.

arxiv-2405-11809.title: Distill-then-prune: An Efficient Compression Framework for Real-time Stereo Matching Network on Edge Devices
arxiv-2405-11809.creator: Baiyu pan, Jichao jiao, Jianxing pang, Jun cheng
arxiv-2405-11809.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Baiyu pan, Jichao jiao, Jianxing pang, Jun cheng. In recent years, numerous real-time stereo matching methods have been introduced, but they often lack accuracy. These methods attempt to improve accuracy by introducing new modules or integrating traditional methods. However, the improvements are only modest. In this paper, we propose a novel strategy by incorporating knowledge distillation and model pruning to overcome the inherent trade-off between speed and accuracy.

arxiv-2508-14781.title: Sideband Spectroscopy in the Strong Driving Regime: Volcano Transparency and Sideband Anomaly
arxiv-2508-14781.creator: Luka Antonić, Sergey Hazanov, Sergei Masis, Daniel Podolsky, Eyal Buks
arxiv-2508-14781.description: Abstract We study the response of a spin to two crossed magnetic fields: a strong and fast transverse field, and a weak and slow longitudinal field. We characterize the sideband response at the sum and the difference of driving frequencies over a broad range of parameters.

arxiv-2512-15673.title: Percolation on random graphs Thanks: The full version of the paper can be accessed at https://arxiv.org/abs/0000.00000
arxiv-2512-15673.creator: Remco van der Hofstad
arxiv-2512-15673.description: Abstract Percolation is a model for random damage to a network. It is one of the simplest models that displays a phase transition : when the network is severely damaged, it falls apart in many small connected components, while if the damage is light, connectivity is hardly affected.

arxiv-2602-10447.title: Bridging the Kinetic-Fluid Gap: Ion-Driven Magnetogenesis to Prime Cosmic Dynamos
arxiv-2602-10447.creator: X. Liu, D. Wu, J. Zhang
arxiv-2602-10447.description: Abstract The origin of cosmic magnetic fields is widely attributed to the amplification of weak seed fields by turbulent dynamos. However, a critical understanding gap remains between the microscopic generation of these seeds and the macroscopic onset of the dynamo.

arxiv-2602-18533.title: Morphological Addressing of Identity Basins in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
arxiv-2602-18533.creator: Andrew Fraser
arxiv-2602-18533.description: Abstract We demonstrate that morphological pressure creates navigable gradients at multiple levels of the text-to-image generative pipeline. In Study 1, we show that identity basins in Stable Diffusion 1.5 can be reliably navigated using morphological descriptors—constituent features like “platinum blonde,” “beauty mark,” and “1950s glamour”—without using the target identity’s name or photographs.

arxiv-2603-02690.creator: Jian Sheng Wang

arxiv-2605-03985.title: Classification of irreducible Harish-Chandra modules over extended Divergence zero Lie algebras
arxiv-2605-03985.creator: Sudipta Mukherjee

pmc-10595472.title: Barriers, facilitators and needs for self-direction in return-to-work: a multi-perspective study
pmc-10595472.creator: B P de Mul, H J de Vries, R van Ooijen, CAM Roelen, S Brouwer
pmc-10595472.description: BackgroundLong-term sickness absence is not only an organizational, but also a societal public health problem. Many sick-listed workers experience challenges in self-directing their return-to-work (RTW), where RTW is considered as a gradual process in which work hours and tasks are gradually increased.

pmc-10702117.title: Sodium-dependent glucose transporter 2 inhibitor alleviates renal lipid deposition and improves renal oxygenation levels in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus patients: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-10702117.creator: Li Zhang, Tongdan Wang, Yan Kong, Haizhen Sun, Yuling Zhang, Junmei Wang, Zhida Wang, Shan Lu, Pei Yu, Saijun Zhou
pmc-10702117.description: BackgroundSodium-dependent glucose transporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) has the advantages of effectively lowering blood glucose levels and improving renal outcomes in diabetic patients. This study evaluated the effect of canagliflozin on intrarenal lipid content and oxygenation in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients.

pmc-11300994.title: Follow-up cancer care in Danish general practice: a questionnaire study
pmc-11300994.creator: Lisa Maria Sele Sætre, Steffi Blach Naamansen, Kirubakaran Balasubramaniam, Jens Søndergaard, Dorte Ejg Jarbøl
pmc-11300994.description: BackgroundThe number of patients who have survived cancer has increased substantially owing to improved cancer treatment. This has reinforced the need for effective strategies for follow-up cancer care in general practice.AimTo investigate the organisation of follow-up cancer care in Danish general practice and to analyse GPs’ self-assessment of competences regarding patients who have survived cancer and late effects.

pmc-11417230.title: The markers of the predictive DNA test for canine hip dysplasia may have a stronger relationship with elbow dysplasia
pmc-11417230.creator: Sena Ardicli, Pelin Yigitgor, Huseyn Babayev, Dogukan Ozen, Berkay Bozkurt, Nursen Senturk, Mehmet Pilli, Hakan Salci, Deniz Seyrek Intas
pmc-11417230.description: Canine hip and elbow dysplasias, which are prevalent orthopedic conditions rooted in developmental and hereditary factors are yet to be comprehensively assessed. This study aimed to address this gap by exploring the prognostic significance of five markers linked to canine hip dysplasia using available genome-wide association studies (GWAS) data.

pmc-12409146.title: Impact of Storage on the Color of a Green Isotonic Beverage With β‐Cyclodextrin/Chlorophyll Complexes
pmc-12409146.creator: Claudio Lombardelli, Ilaria Benucci, Chiara Pippolini, Rosita Marabottini, Marco Esti, Narashans Alok Sagar
pmc-12409146.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study analyzes the stability of chlorophyll (Chl) from unsold spinach in isotonic beverages, comparing the pigment in its free form with that encapsulated in β‐cyclodextrin (β‐CD), after determining the inclusion ratio of 1:1. Stability was monitored for 14 days for the crude extract and 30 days for the lyophilized powder under different storage conditions (dark, natural light, and UV light, at 4°C and 25°C).

pmc-12961305.title: Cortical integration of tactile inputs distributed across timescales
pmc-12961305.creator: Wenyu Wan, K Richard Ridderinkhof, Arko Ghosh
pmc-12961305.description: Sensory experiences in the real world cut across timescales from milliseconds to seconds. Emerging evidence suggests that somatosensory processing is sensitive to the temporal structure of the stimuli in the sub-second scale, yet only a few select ranges within this scale have been studied.

pmc-13081468.title: The impact of received support on distressing experiences among nurses as second victims: the mediating role of psychological capital
pmc-13081468.creator: Wei Zong, Jing Qiu, Lin Chen, Meng Zhang, Xiaobin Wang, Xiangguang Yin, Jing Wei
pmc-13081468.description: BackgroundAll healthcare professionals are potentially susceptible to becoming second victims of adverse events during the course of their careers. Nurses, as second victims, frequently encounter a series of distressing experiences, including anxiety, depression, tension, fear, sleep disorders, and occupational burnout.

pmc-13273584.title: Assessment of synergistic effects of ultrasonication, ozonation and their combination with aloe vera active edible coating containing spirulina and turmeric extracts on preservation of fresh-cut apples
pmc-13273584.creator: Samran Khalid, Kashmala Chaudhary, Ahmed Fathy Ghazal, Abderrahmane Aït-Kaddour, Marwa Ezz El-Din Ibrahim, Rana Muhammad Aadil
